# Configure password authentication

The [password auth method](/boundary/docs/domain-model/auth-methods#password-auth-method-attributes) authenticates users against credentials that Boundary stores and manages directly. Unlike OIDC or LDAP, password auth methods do not require an external identity provider, which makes them useful for initial setup and for accounts that do not need to authenticate against a third-party system.

Password auth methods do not have an operational state. Unlike OIDC and LDAP auth methods, they are always available for authentication and do not need to be activated.

## Create a password auth method

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="UI" group="ui">

1. Log in to Boundary.
1. Select the scope in which you want to create the auth method.
1. Select **Auth Methods**, then click **New**.
1. Select **Password**, and complete the following fields:
   - **Name**: (Optional) An optional name for identification purposes.
   - **Description**: (Optional) An optional description of the auth method.
1. Click **Save**.

</Tab>
<Tab heading="CLI" group="cli">

```shell-session
$ boundary auth-methods create password \
  -scope-id $SCOPE_ID \
  -name "corp-password" \
  -description "Password auth method for corp scope"
```

By default, login names must be lowercase and at least 3 characters, and passwords must be at least 8 characters. Set `-min-login-name-length` or `-min-password-length` to change these requirements.

Refer to the [auth-methods create](/boundary/docs/commands/auth-methods/create) command documentation for more information.

</Tab>
<Tab heading="Terraform" group="terraform">

Apply the following Terraform configuration:

```hcl
resource "boundary_auth_method_password" "corp_password" {
  name        = "corp-password"
  description = "Password auth method for corp scope"
  scope_id    = "SCOPE_ID"
}
```

Replace `scope_id` with the ID of the scope in which you want to create the auth method.

Refer to the [boundary_auth_method](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/boundary/latest/docs/resources/auth_method) resource documentation for more information.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Create an account

An [account](/boundary/docs/domain-model/accounts#password-account-attributes) links a login name and password to an auth method. If you do not set a password, Boundary disables the account.

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="UI" group="ui">

1. Select the password auth method you created.
1. Select the **Accounts** tab, then click **New**.
1. Complete the following fields:
   - **Name**: (Optional) An optional name for identification purposes.
   - **Description**: (Optional) An optional description of the account.
   - **Login Name**: (Required) The lowercase login name for the account.
   - **Password**: (Optional) The account's password.
1. Click **Save**.

</Tab>
<Tab heading="CLI" group="cli">

```shell-session
$ boundary accounts create password \
  -auth-method-id $PASSWORD_AUTH_METHOD_ID \
  -login-name "myuser" \
  -password "env://BOUNDARY_ACCOUNT_PASSWORD" \
  -name "myuser-account"
```

Pass the password using an environment variable or file reference instead of typing it directly on the command line.

</Tab>
<Tab heading="Terraform" group="terraform">

```hcl
resource "boundary_account_password" "myuser" {
  name           = "myuser-account"
  description    = "Password account for myuser"
  auth_method_id = boundary_auth_method_password.corp_password.id
  login_name     = "myuser"
  password       = "PASSWORD"
}
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Create and link a user

Boundary automatically creates a user the first time someone authenticates successfully using a scope's [primary auth method](/boundary/docs/authentication#what-is-a-primary-auth-method). If the password auth method is not primary for its scope, or you want to control user creation explicitly, create the user and link it to the account yourself.

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="UI" group="ui">

1. Select **Users**, then click **New**.
1. Complete the **Name** and **Description** fields, and select **Save**.
1. From the user's **Accounts** tab, select **Manage**, then select **Add Accounts**.
1. Select the account you created, and select **Add Accounts**.

</Tab>
<Tab heading="CLI" group="cli">

1. Create the user. 

  ```shell-session
  $ boundary users create \
    -scope-id $SCOPE_ID \
    -name "myuser" \
    -description "My user resource"
  ```

1. Link the user with an account. 

  ```shell-session
  $ boundary users set-accounts \
    -id $USER_ID \
    -account $ACCOUNT_ID
  ```

</Tab>
<Tab heading="Terraform" group="terraform">

```hcl
resource "boundary_user" "myuser" {
  name        = "myuser"
  description = "My user resource"
  account_ids = [boundary_account_password.myuser.id]
  scope_id    = "SCOPE_ID"
}
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Authenticate

```shell-session
$ boundary authenticate password \
  -auth-method-id $PASSWORD_AUTH_METHOD_ID \
  -login-name "myuser"
```

## More information

- Refer to the [Auth method](/boundary/docs/domain-model/auth-methods#password-auth-method-attributes) and [Account](/boundary/docs/domain-model/accounts#password-account-attributes) domain model topics for the full list of password auth method and account attributes.
- Refer to [Permissions in Boundary](/boundary/docs/rbac) to learn how to assign roles and grants to a user.
- To learn more about managing users, refer to the CLI [`users`](/boundary/docs/commands/users) topic or the API [User service](/boundary/api-docs/user-service) topic.
